description: Korean historical and alternate-history fiction set in Joseon or the Korean Empire, with precise court, military, diplomatic, and period terminology.

style: Natural, polished English historical prose faithful to the Korean source.
Preserve narrator voice, humor, characterization, hierarchy, and shifts between courtly, military, diplomatic, and casual registers, including a modern narrator's voice inside a historical setting.
Keep Joseon institutions, offices, and customs conceptually Korean in clear English rather than replacing them with Western or Chinese equivalents.
terminology_preservation_rules: Keep royal titles, forms of address, court offices, government bodies, military ranks and units, factions, treaties, historical events, and recurring period terms stable.
Keep 전하 (Your Highness) and 폐하 (Your Majesty) distinct; the change from kingdom to empire is meaningful.
Distinguish formal named concepts from ordinary vocabulary and reject generic objects, actions, and one-off descriptions.
translation_policy.pinyin_preference: Do not apply Chinese pinyin policy to Korean. Korean personal and place names use Revised Romanization, surname first, except well-known historical names with an established English form. Chinese names use pinyin, Japanese names use Hepburn without long-vowel marks, and Western names keep their original spelling.
translation_policy.semantic_translation_preference: Translate Joseon offices, institutions, ranks, and titles into their standard English renderings, never bare romanization or a Western substitute; keep Korean words that English dictionaries already use, such as yangban, and translate the rest.

terminology_distinctions: Korean names and places use Revised Romanization, surname first, unless a well-known historical name has an established English form.

Joseon offices and institutions take standard English renderings: 승정원 Royal Secretariat, 도승지 Chief Royal Secretary, 의정부 State Council, 영의정 Chief State Councillor; no Western substitutes such as Prime Minister.
전하 is Your Highness and 폐하 is Your Majesty; never merge them.
Chinese names use pinyin, Japanese names use Hepburn without long-vowel marks, Western names keep their original spelling.
Keep real historical people, treaties, and events under their established English names.

review_priorities: Korean, Chinese, Japanese, and Western name spellings under the profile's romanization rules.
Royal titles and forms of address, especially Your Highness versus Your Majesty.
Court offices, government bodies, military ranks and units in standard English renderings.
States, factions, organizations, treaties, historical events, and locations.
Named weapons, ships, and recurring period or technical terms.
Reject generic vocabulary, ordinary objects, and one-off descriptions.
